That which is laminated, golden in color, with laminas that flake off and are as if lying on one another, and which is pure must be thought to be excellent. Such is the one formed in Mysia, at the Hellespont. There are two kinds of it. The one is as described above; the other is %%διφρυγές “twice roasted.” See Dsc. Bk. V, 77. lumpy, bright red in color, and it is brought from Pontus and Cappadocia. This kind ranks second. It is baked this way: after putting it in a fresh clay vessel, place it on red-hot coals and stir it continuously until it becomes red-hot and changes color; then cool, pound, and store. It has putrefactive and escharotic properties with burning and intense biting. It belongs to the group of astringents. It is also depilatory.

entry_gr: σανδαράκην δὲ προκριτέον τὴν κατακορῆ, πυρράν, [εὔθλαστον], εὐλέαντόν τε καὶ καθαράν, κινναβαρίζουσαν τὴν χρόαν, ἔτι δὲ θειώδη ἀποφοράν ἔχουσαν. δύναμιν δὲ ἔχει καὶ ὄπτησιν τὴν αὐτὴν τῷ ἀρσενικῷ. θεραπεύει δὲ καὶ ἀλωπεκίας ἀναλημφθεῖσα ῥητίνη, καὶ λεπροὺς ὄνυχας σὺν πίσσῃ ἀφίστησι, καὶ πρὸς φθειριάσεις σὺν ἐλαίῳ ποιεῖ, φύματά τε σὺν στέατι διαφορεῖ. ἁρμόζει δὲ καὶ πρὸς 2 τὰ ἐν ῥισὶ καὶ στόματι ἕλκη καὶ τὰ λοιπά, καὶ πρὸς ἐξανθήματα σὺν ῥοδίνῳ καὶ πρὸς κονδυλώματα· δίδοται καὶ ἐμπυικοῖς σὺν οἰνομέλιτι, καὶ ὑποθυμιᾶται σὺν ῥητίνῃ καὶ πρὸς παλαιὰν βῆχα διὰ σίφωνος ἑλκομένου τοῦ ἀτμοῦ τῷ στόματι, φωνήν τε ἀποκαθαίρει ἐκλειχομένη μετὰ μέλιτος, καὶ ἀσθματικοῖς σὺν ῥητίνη καταπότιον δίδοται.
entry_en: 1. You must select arsenic sulfide that is deep red, [friable,] easily triturated and clean, having the color of cinnabar, and also smelling like sulfur. It has the same properties and it is baked the same way as yellow orpiment. But in combination with pine resin it also treats bald spots, with pitch it removes psoriatic nails, with olive oil it is good for pediculosis, and with animal fat it dissolves tumors. 2. It is also suitable for sores in the nose, mouth, and for the rest of sores, for pustules with unguent of roses, and for callous lumps. It is given with honey mixed with wine to people who suffer from internal abscesses, it is burned with pine resin to produce smoke from below and the steam is drawn with the mouth through a siphon for an old cough, it clears the voice if sucked with honey, and it is given to asthmatics with pine resin as a little pill.

var_par_prod_gr: ὦτα, Αἰγυπτία, χαλκῖτις, λευκή, στρογγύλη, σχιστή, ὑγρά
entry_gr: στυπτηρίας δὲ σχεδὸν πᾶν εἶδος ἐπὶ τῶν αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ Αἰγύπτῳ μετάλλων εὐρίσκεται· γεννᾶται δὲ καὶ ἐν ἄλλοις τόποις, ὡς ἐν Μήλῳ, ἐν Μακεδονίᾳ, ἐν Λιπάραις, Σαρδόνι. Ἱεραπόλει τῆς Φρυγίας, Λιβύῃ, Ἀρμενίᾳ, καὶ ἐν ἄλλοις δὲ τόποις πλείοσιν ὥσπερ ἡ μίλτος. ἐστι δʼ αὐτῆς εἴδη πλεῖστα, πρὸς δὲ ἰατρικὴν χρῆσιν λαμβάνεται ἡ σχιστή τε καὶ ἡ στρογγύλη καὶ ἡ ὑγρά. ἀρίστη δὲ 2 ὑπάρχει ἡ σχιστή, καὶ ταύτης ἡ πρόσφατος καὶ λευκὴ ἄγαν καὶ βαρύοζος, στύφουσά τε εὐτόνως καὶ ἄλιθος, ἔτι δὲ οὐ πεπιεσμένη βωληδὸν ἢ σχιδακηδόν, ἀλλὰ διεξασμένη κατὰ μονάδας πολιαῖς θριξὶν ἐμφερεῖς, οἵα ἐστὶν ἡ λεγομένη τριχῖτις, γεννωμένη δὲ ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ. εὑρίσκεται δὲ λίθος ἐμφερὴς αὐτῇ ἄγαν, ὃν διακριτέον τῷ τῆς γεύσεως κριτηρίῳ, μὴ στύφοντα. τῆς δὲ στρογγύλης ἡ μὲν χειροποίητος ἀδόκιμος ὑπάρχει. 3 γνωρίζεται δὲ ἐκ τοῦ σχήματος. παραλημπτέα δὲ ἂν εἵη ἡ φυσικῶς στρογγύλη καὶ πομφολυγώδης, ὑπόλευκός τε καὶ στύφουσα ἐρρωμένως, ἔτι δὲ ἐπὶ ποσόν τι ὠχρότητος ἅμα καὶ λιπαρίας ἔχουσα· πρὸς δὲ τούτοις ἄλιθός τε καὶ εὐθρυβὴς καὶ γένει Μηλία ἢ Αἰγυπτία. τῆς δὲ ὑγρᾶς τὴν μάλιστα διαφανῆ προκριτέον καὶ γαλακτώδη, ὁμαλήν τε καὶ διόλου χυλώδη, ἔτι δὲ ἄλιθον καὶ πυρῶδες ἀπονέουσαν. 4 δύναμιν δὲ ἔχουσι θερμαντικήν, στυπτικήν, τῶν ἐπισκοτούντων ταῖς κόραις ἀποκαθαρτικήν, τήκουσι δὲ καὶ τὰς ἐπὶ τῶν βλεφάρων σάρκας καὶ τὰ ἄλλα ὑπερσαρκώματα. ἐνεργεστέραν δὲ τῆς στρογγύλης τὴν σχιστὴν ἡγητέον· καίονται δὲ καὶ ὀπτῶνται ὡς χαλκῖτις. ἴσχουσι δὲ καὶ σηπεδόνας καὶ αἱμορραγίας, οὖλά τε πλαδῶντα στέλλουσι, καὶ ὀδόντας σειομένους κρατύνουσι σὺν ὄξει ἢ μέλιτι. 5 ἄφθας δὲ ὠφελοῦσι σὺν μέλιτι καὶ ἐξανθήματα, καὶ ῥεύματα ἐν ὠσὶ σὺν πολυγόνου χυλῷ. λέπραις δὲ ἁρμόζουσι σὺν κράμβης χυλῷ ἢ σὺν μέλιτι ἑψηθεῖσαι καὶ κνησμοῖς, ὄνυξί τε λεπροῖς καὶ πτερυγίοις καὶ χιμέτλαις σὺν ὕδατι καταιονούμεναι· σὺν τρυγὶ δὲ ὄξους καταχριόμεναι καὶ μετὰ κηκίδος ἴσης κεκαυμένης πρὸς φαγεδαινικά. πρὸς δὲ νομὰς σὺν ἁλσὶ διπλοῖς, πιτυριάσεσι δὲ σὺν ὄρρῷ 6 πίσσης καταχριόμεναι, κονίδων τε καὶ φθειρῶν καὶ πυρικαύτων σὺν ὕδατι καταχριόμεναι βοήθημα, οἰδήμασί τε καὶ μασχαλῶν καὶ βουβώνων δυσωδίαις κατάχριστοι. πρὸς δὲ ἔμμηνα καὶ πρὸς ἀσυλλημψίαν συνεργεῖ πρὸ τῆς συνόδου παρατεθεῖσα τῷ στόματι τῆς ὑστέρας καὶ ἔμβρυα ἐκτινάσσει· ἐπουλίσι τε καὶ σταφυλαῖς καὶ παρισθμίοις ἐπιτήδειοι καὶ στόματι, καὶ πρὸς ὦτα καὶ αἰδοῖα σὺν μέλιτι ἐπίχριστοι.
entry_en: 1. Nearly every kind of alum is found in the same mines in Egypt. But alum also occurs in other places, as in Melos, Macedonia, Lipari, Sardinia, Hierapolis of Phrygia, Libya, Armenia, and in many other places, just like red earth. There are many kinds of it, but for medicinal purposes they use that which is cloven, round, and moist. 2. Outstanding is the cloven, and of this one, that which is fresh, very white, oppressive in smell, powerfully astringent, and free of stones; moreover, it should not be compressed like a clump of earth nor spindly, but it should be arranged in strands resembling gray hairs; the one called trichitis,'^^ which occurs in Egypt, is of that sort. There is, however, a stone that resembles it a great deal which you must identify by the criterion of taste because it is not astringent. Of the round, the one that is man-made is unsatisfactory. It is recognizable from its shape. 3. You must use that which is naturally round and which is like bubbles, whitish, and extremely astringent; moreover, it should have a touch of paleness and at the same time some glitter; in addition to these characteristics it should be free of stones, crumbling, and either Melian or Egyptian of origin. But of the moist you must choose that which is very translucent and milky, smooth and moist throughout; moreover, you must choose it free of stones and emanating heat. 4. They have properties that warm, that are astringent, that clear off the elements that cast a shadow over the pupils of the eyes, and that reduce both the flesh on the eyelids and other overgrown fleshes. The one that is cloven must be regarded more effective than the round. Alums are calcined and baked like rock alum. They stem both putrid humors and hemorrhages, they tighten flaccid gums, and with vinegar or honey they strengthen loose teeth. 5. They are beneficial with honey for thrush and for pustules, and with the juice of polygonon^ for ear rheums. They are suitable for leprosies and for itches when boiled with cabbage juice or with honey, and they are poured with water over scaly nails, fleshy excrescences, and chilblains. They are suitable for cancerous conditions smeared on with vinegar lees and with an equal amount of burned oak galls. 6. For spreading ulcers, they are anointed with twice as much salt, for dandruff, with the watery part of wood-tar, and <they are helpful> when rubbed on with water for nits, pediculosis, and bums; they are also used as ointments for swellings and for the bad odors of armpits and groins. They help to induce menstruation and for barrenness when placed at the mouth of the uterus prior to sexual intercourse, and they expel embryos/fetuses. They are also suitable for growths on the %%Akin to 0pi4, rpixog, “hair.” Ordinarily TtoWyovov is qualified by appev, “knot-grass,” Polygonum aviculare, or QfiXu, “mare’s tail” Hippuris vulgaris. gums, for swollen uvulas, for the tonsils, the mouth, and they are also smeared with honey for the ears and the genitalia.

entry_gr: θεῖον δὲ ἄριστον ἡγητέον τὸ ἄπυρον καὶ λαμπυρίζον τῇ χρόᾳ, διαφανές τε καὶ ἄλιθον, τοῦ δὲ πεπυρωμένου τὸ χλωρόν τε καὶ εὐλιπές. γεννᾶται δὲ πλεῖστον ἐν Μήλῳ καὶ Λιπάραις. θερμαίνει δὲ τὸ προειρημένον καὶ διαφορεῖ καὶ πεπαίνει ταχέως, βῆχάς τε καὶ ἐμπύους καὶ ἀσθματικοὺς ὠφελεῖ ἐν ᾠῷ λαμβανόμενον καὶ ὑποθυμιμώμενον. πρὸς δὲ τούτοις ἔμβρυα 2 κατασπᾷ ὑποθυμιαθέν, καὶ λέπρας, ἔτι δὲ λειχῆνας καὶ ὄνυχας λεπροὺς αἴρει τετεβινθίνῃ μιγὲν ῥητίνῃ. σὺν ὄξει δὲ καταχριόμενον ποιεῖ μὲν καὶ πρὸς λέπρας, αἴρει δὲ καὶ ἀλφούς. ἰᾶται δὲ καὶ σκορπίων πληγὰς μιγὲν ῥητίνῃ, σὺν ὄξει δὲ καταχριόμενον θαλαττίου δράκοντος καὶ σκορπίου πληγὴν παραιτεῖται· παύει καὶ τοὺς καθʼ ὅλον τὸ σῶμα κνησμοὺς σὺν νίτρῳ σμηχόμενον. ἀποκαθαίρει δὲ καὶ ἴκτερον κοχλιαρίου πλῆθος ἐπιπασσομένου τῷ ποτῷ ἢ μετὰ ᾠοῦ ῥοφητοῦ λαμβανόμενον· καὶ πρὸς κόρυζαν δὲ καὶ πρὸς κατάρρουν ποιεῖ, καὶ ἱδρῶτας στέλλει καταπασσόμενον, καὶ ποδαγρικοὺς σὺν νίτρῳ καὶ ὕδατι καταχρισθὲν ὠφελεῖ, καὶ δυσηκοίαν ὑποθυμιώμενον διὰ σίφωνος. θεραπεύει καὶ ληθαργικοὺς ὑποθυμιώμενον, αἱμορραγίας τε ἴσχει, θλάσεις τε ὤτων σὺν οἴνῳ καὶ σμύρνῃ καταχριόμενον ἰᾶται.
entry_en: 1. Sulfur that has not been burned must be judged to be excellent when it is of a shiny color, transparent, and free of stones, but of the sulfur that has been burned, it is the pale green and very fat that is excellent. Much sulfur is produced on Melos and on the Lipari islands. The sulfur mentioned first, warms, disperses, causes quick ripening, is good for coughs, for people who suffer from abscesses, and for asthmatics when taken in an egg and when burned so as to produce smoke. 2. In addition to these uses, it does draw embryos/fetuses when burned so as to produce smoke from below; moreover, it removes leprosies, lichen-like eruptions of the skin, and psoriatic nails when mixed with turpentine resin. Smeared on with vinegar, it is good for leprosies and it removes dull-white leprosies. Mixed with pine resin, it treats the strokes of scorpions and assuages the stroke of the great weever and of the sea scorpion when laid on with vinegar. Used as a wash with soda, it stops itching throughout the body. 3. It clears away jaundice when an amount of one spoonful is sprinkled on a drink or is taken with an egg that can be supped up. It is good both for a running nose and for catarrh, it controls perspiration when used like dusting powder, it benefits the gouty when smeared on with soda and water, and it is beneficial for hardness of hearing when, as it smolders, its smoke is siphoned into the ears. It even treats people affected by lethargic fever when burned to produce smoke, and it stems hemorrhages and heals bruised ears when anointed with wine and myrrh.

entry_gr: κίσηριν δὲ προκριτέον τὴν κούφην ἄγαν καὶ πολύκενον, σχιστήν τε καὶ ἄλιθον, ἔτι δὲ ψαθυράν τε καὶ λευκήν. καυστέον δὲ οὕτως· λαβὼν αὐτῆς ὁπόσον ἂν θέλῃς διαπύροις ἔγκρυψον ἄνθραξιν· ὡς δʼ ἂν ἐκπυρωθῇ, ἀνελόμενος σβέσον οἴνῳ εὐώδει καὶ πάλιν πυρώσας σβέσον· τὸ δὲ τρίτον διʼ ἑαυτῆς ἔασον ψυγῆναι καὶ ἀπόθου καὶ χρῶ. δύναμιν δὲ ἔχει στυπτικήν [τε] καὶ σμηκτικὴν οὔλων καὶ 2 ἀποκαθαρτικὴν τῶν ἐπισκοτούντων ταῖς κόραις μετὰ τοῦ θερμαίνειν, πληρωτικήν τε ἑλκῶν καὶ κατουλωτικήν, ἔτι δὲ καὶ κατασταλτικὴν ὑπεροχῶν καὶ σμηκτικὴν ὀδόντων λεία καὶ σώματος εἰς ψίλωσιν τριχῶν. Θεόφραστος (h. pl. IX 17, 3) δὲ ἱστορεῖ, ἐὰν εἰς ζέοντα οἴνου πίθον καθῇ τις κίσηριν, παύεσθαι παραχρῆμα τὴν ζέσιν.
entry_en: 1. One must prefer pumice stone that is very light and porous, cloven and free of stones. Additionally, it should be friable and white. You must bum it this way; after taking as much of it as you wish, burry it among very hot coals. When it has caught fire, take it out and quench it with fragrant wine, and after burning it again, quench it. After you have done so three times, let it cool by itself, store, and use. 2. It has properties that contract, clean the gums, purge the elements that cast a shadow over the pupils of the eyes by way of warming, fill up and cicatrize sores, also reduce excrescences, clean the teeth and the body when used as a powder, and are suitable for the removal of hair. Theophrastus'*'* reports that if one dropped pumice stone into a boiling cask of wine, the boiling immediately stops.

entry_gr: τῶν δὲ ἁλῶν ἐνεργέστατον μέν ἐστι τὸ ὀρυκτόν. τούτου δὲ κοινῶς μὲν τὸ λευκὸν ἄλιθον καὶ διαφανές, πυκνόν τε καὶ ὁμαλὸν τῇ συγκρίσει· ἰδίως δὲ τὸ ἀμμωνιακὸν τῷ γένει, σχιστόν τε καὶ εὐθείας τὰς διαφύσεις ἔχον. τοῦ δὲ θαλασσίου τὸ πυκνὸν παραλημπτέον καὶ λευκὸν καὶ ὁμαλόν. κάλλιστον δὲ ἐν Κύπρῳ καὶ Σαλαμῖνι τῆς Κύπρου γίνεται καὶ ἐν Μεγάροις, εἶτα ἐν Σικελίᾳ καὶ Λιβύῃ, καὶ ἐν τοῖς προειρημένοις τὰ λιμναῖα προκριτέον· εὐτονώτατον δέ ἐστιν αὐτοῦ τὸ Φρύγιον, καλούμενον δὲ Τατταῖον. 2 δύναμιν δὲ ἔχουσι κοινῶς οἱ προειρημένοι ἅλες ὄντες πολύχρηστοι στυπτικήν τε καὶ σμηκτικὴν καὶ ἀποκαθαρτικὴν καὶ διαχυτικήν, ἔτι δὲ κατασταλτικὴν καὶ ἐσχαρωτικήν, τῷ μᾶλλον καὶ ἧττον διαφέροντες. εἰσὶ δὲ καὶ σηπεδόνων ἐφεκτικοὶ καὶ σμήξεσι ψωρικαῖς μείγνυνται· στέλλουσι καὶ τὰς ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς ὑπεροχὰς καὶ πτερύγια τήκουσι, καὶ τὰς ἄλλας δὲ ὑπερσαρκώσεις, κλυσμοῖς τε εὔθετοι καὶ κόπου λυτήριοι σὺν ἐλαίῳ συγχριόμενοι καὶ πρὸς τὰ οἰδήματα τῶν ὑδρωπικῶν, πυρία τε ἡ διʼ αὐτῶν ἐν σακκίοις πραυντικὴ ἀλγημάτων. 3 καὶ κνησμοὺς δὲ παύουσι μετʼ ἐλαίου καὶ ὄξους συγχριόμενοι παρὰ πυρί, ἄχρι ἂν ἱδρώσωσιν· ὁμοίως καὶ λέπρας καὶ λειχῆνας καὶ ψώρας συναγχικούς τε κουφίζουσι σὺν μέλιτι καὶ ὄξει καὶ ἐλαίῳ διαχριόμενοι. πρὸς δὲ παρίσθμια καὶ κιονίδας σὺν μέλιτι καὶ ἄφθας καὶ οὔλων πλάδον, καὶ πρὸς φαγεδαίνας σὺν ἀλφίτῳ κεκαυμένοι καταπλάσσονται.
entry_en: 1. The most effective salt is that which is mined and of this kind, in general, that which is white, free of stones, translucent, dense, smooth in its formation, particularly the Ammonian*\"’ in origin, that can be split, and that has straight cracks. But you must select sea salt that is dense, white, and smooth. Excellent is salt produced in Cyprus, especially in Salamis of Cyprus, and in Megara, then that produced in Sicily and Libya, and among the above mentioned, salt from marshlands is preferable. Of this type, the Phrygian, which is called Tattaion, is very strong. 2. The salts mentioned above, which are highly useful and differ in varying degrees, have in common properties that are astringent, detersive, that cleanse, and that dissolve; furthermore, they are capable of suppressing and of forming eschars. They can also stop putrid humors and they are mixed with itch salves; they check small protuberances on the eyes, they draw in membranes that grow over the eyes from their inner comers and the other types of flesh overgrowths, they are suitable to put in clysters, they reheve weariness when smeared on with olive oil, they are good for the swellings of the dropsical, and a hot compress of salts in little bags allays pains. 3. They also stop itching when smeared on by the fire with olive oil and vinegar until the patients sweat. When laid on with honey, vinegar, and olive oil they relieve likewise leprosies, lichen-like eruptions on the skin, itching, and sore throats. But for tonsillitis and for inflammations of the uvula they are plastered on with honey, and for thrush, flaccid gums, and cankers they are applied burned with barley groats. %%Theophrastus, H. P., IX, 17, 3. This is rock salt mined near the temple of Jupiter Ammon, in Libya. 4. For strokes of scorpions, they are laid on with linseed; for viper stings, with oregano, honey, and hyssop; for the sting of the asp, with pitch or with oil of Syrian cedar or with honey; for the bite of the millipede, with vinegar and honey, also for the sting of wasps and of earth-wasps; but for pimples on the head, warty excrescences, and growths, they are combined with calf s suet. 5. With raisins or with beef suet or with honey, they dissolve small abscesses and testicular swelling; with oregano and leaven, they cause <small abscesses> to mature faster. Tied ground up in a linen cloth and dipped in vinegar, they help those bitten by crocodiles, the bitten parts being constricted with tourniquets; they also help those bitten by wild animals, and for facial bruises with honey, and for drinking opium juice, and for mushrooms when drunk with a mixture of vinegar and honey. 6. They are good with flour and honey for sprains, they prevent bums from blistering if plastered on with oil, they are similarly applied on the gouty, they are applied with vinegar for earaches, and they check erysipelas and shingles when plastered on with vinegar or when smeared on with hyssop. You must bum them by placing them in a clay vessel, seal it carefully so that they do not fly off, and bury the vessel in coals until completely burned. 7. But some wrap quarried salt in dough, bury it in coals, and leave it until the dough is thoroughly burned. It is possible to bum even common salt this way: after rinsing it with water once and letting it dry out, place it in a vessel and, covering it with a lid, bum it from below, moving about the pot until the salt no longer leaps up.

entry_gr: ἁλὸς ἄχνη ἐπίψημά ἐστιν ἁλὸς ἀφρῶδες, εὑρισκόμενον ἐπὶ τῶν πετριδίων, δύναμιν ἔχον τὴν αὐτὴν τοῖς ἁλσίν.
entry_en: Salt froth is the foamy scraping of salt found on the small stones; it has the same properties as salt.

entry_gr: ἅλμη τὴν αὐτὴν ἔχει τοῖς ἁλσὶν ἐνέργειαν στυπτικήν, σμηκτικήν, λεπτυντικήν, δυσεντερικοῖς τέ ἐστι τοῖς καὶ νομὴν ἔχουσιν ἔγκλυσμα καὶ ἰσχιάδων χρονίων, πρός τε τὰς καταντλήσεις ἁρμόζει, ἐφ᾿ ὧν θάλαττά ἐστι χρησίμη.
entry_en: Brine has the same activity as salt; it is astringent, detersive, and it thins; it is a clyster for dysenteries, for those who have spreading ulcers as well as chronic hip ailments, and it is suitable to use as rinses on those to whom seawater is useful.

entry_gr: ἄνθος δὲ ἁλὸς καταρρεῖ μὲν τῷ Νείλῳ ποταμῷ. ἐφίσταται δὲ λίμναις τισί. παραλημπτέον δὲ τὸ κροκίζον τῇ χρόᾳ, ὑποδυσῶδες ὥσπερ γάρος, ἐνίοτε δὲ καὶ δυσωδέστερον μᾶλλον, καὶ τῇ γεύσει δηκτικώτατον καὶ ὑπολίπαρον· τὸ δὲ ἔμμιλτον ἢ θρόμβους ἔχον φαῦλον ἡγητέον· ἔτι τὸ ἀκέραιον ἐλαίῳ συνανίεται μόνῳ, τὸ δὲ δεδολωμένον ἐκ μέρους καὶ ὕδατι. 2 ποιεῖ δὲ πρὸς τὰ κακοήθη καὶ φαγεδαινικὰ ἕλκη καὶ νομὰς τὰς ἐν αἰδοίοις, ὦτά τε πυορροοῦντα καὶ ἀμβλυωπίας, οὐλάς τε καὶ λευκώματα· μείγνυται καὶ ἐμπλάστροις καὶ μύροις εἰς χρῶσιν, ὡς καὶ τῷ ῥοδίνῳ. ἔστι δὲ καὶ ἱδρώτων κινητικὸν καὶ κοιλίας ταρακτικὸν σὺν οἴνῳ καὶ ὕδατι λημφθέν, κακοστόμαχον δέ· μείγνυται καὶ ἀκόποις καὶ σμήγμασι πρὸς τριχῶν λεπτυσμόν, καὶ καθόλου ἐστὶ δριμύ, πυρωτικὸν ὥσπερ οἱ ἅλες.
entry_en: 1. Salt efflorescence/salt scum flows down the river Nile and settles on top of certain marshes. You must take it saffron colored, smelling somewhat rank like garum, occasionally smelling even more foul, biting in taste, and being somewhat greasy. But if it is tinged with red or if it is lumpy, it must be considered inferior. Moreover, when pure it is soluble only in oil, but the adulterated is partly soluble even in water. 2. It is good for malignant and cancerous sores, for spreading ulcers in the genitalia, for purulent ears, for dim-sightedness, for scars, and for leucomas. It is mixed with plasters and with unguents for coloration, as it is also mixed with unguent of roses. It sets perspiration in motion, it upsets the bowel when taken with wine and water, and it is bad for the stomach. It is mixed with analgesics and with soaps for thinning hair, and, in general, it is harsh and bums like salt.

entry_gr: νίτρον δὲ προκριτέον τὸ κοῦφον καὶ ῥοδωπὸν ἢ λευκὸν τὴν χρόαν, κατατετρημένον, οἱονεὶ σπογγῶδες· τοιοῦτον δέ ἐστι τὸ ἐκ τῶν Βρυγῶν. ἀφρὸς δὲ νίτρου ἄριστος μὲν εἶναι δοκεῖ ὁ κουφότατος καὶ πλακώδης, εὔθρυπτός τε καὶ ἐμπόρφυρος καὶ ἀφρώδης, ἔτι δὲ δηκτικός, οἷός ἐστιν ὁ ἐκ Φιλαδελφίας κομιζόμενος τῆς ἐν Λυδίᾳ· δευτερεύει δὲ ὁ Αἰγύπτιος, γεννᾶται δὲ καὶ ἐν Μαγνησίᾳ τῆς Καρίας. δύναμιν δὲ ἔχει καὶ καῦσιν οὗτός τε καὶ τὸ νίτρον ἁλσὶν ἐμφερῆ· 2 ἐκ περισσοῦ δὲ τὸ νίτρον καὶ στρόφους παύει λεανθὲν μετὰ κυμίνου καὶ ποθὲν μετὰ ὑδρομέλιτος ἢ μετὰ ἑψήματος ἤ τινος τῶν διαφορεῖν δυναμένων πνεύματα, οἷον πηγάνου ἢ ἀνήθου. ἔστι δὲ καὶ περιοδικῶν σύγχρισμα πρὸ τῆς ὑπόπτου προσβολῆς· μείγνυται καὶ διαφορητικαῖς καὶ ἐπισπαστικαῖς καὶ λεπρικαῖς ἐμπλάστροις. 3 σὺν ὕδατι δὲ ἢ οἴνῳ ἐγχεόμενον ἐμπνευματώσεις τε καὶ ἢχους ὤτων ἰᾶται καὶ πυορροίας· καθαίρει δὲ καὶ ῥύπον σὺν ὄξει ἐγχεόμενον, κυνοδήκτους τε ἰᾶται σὺν στέατι ὀνείῳ ἢ ὑείῳ· ἀναστομοῖ δὲ καὶ δοθιῆνας ἀναλημφθὲν τερμινθίνῃ ῥητίνῃ. μετὰ σύκων δὲ ὑδρωπικῶν ἐστι κατάπλασμα, σὺν μέλιτι δὲ ἐγχριόμενον ὀξυδερκές, καὶ πρὸς μύκητας σὺν ὀξυκράτῳ ποθὲν ἁρμόζει, πρὸς δὲ βουπρήστεις σὺν ὕδατι, πρὸς 4 ταύρειον δὲ αἷμα σὺν σιλφίῳ· ἀτροφοῦσί τε χρήσιμον κατάπλασμα, παρακμάζουσί τε ὀπισθοτονικοῖς πάθεσι σὺν κηρωτῇ καὶ στρέμμασι· μείγνυται καὶ ἄρτῳ ὠφελίμως ἐπὶ τῶν τὴν γλῶτταν παραλελυμένων. ἔν ιοι δὲ καίουσι τά προειρημένα ἐπ ἄνθρακας πεπυρωμένους ἀπερεισόμενοι, προυποκειμένου καινοῦ ὀστράκου, ἕως ἂν ἐκπυρωθῇ.
entry_en: 1. One must choose soda that is light and either rosy or white in color, having holes, as if it were a spongy substance. Such is the one from Bryges.\"'26 dcppog virpou. Foam of soda seems to be of excellent quality if it is very light, flaky, crumbly, inclining to purple, foamy, and biting. Such is the one brought from Philadelphia in Lydia. The Egyptian is ranked second. It occurs also in Magnesia of Caria. 2. Both it and soda have the same properties and they are burned the same way as salt; however, soda can to a far greater degree stop colic when triturated with cumin and drunk with hydromel or with must or with any of the substances that can dissipate flatulence, such as rue or dill. It is also an ointment for intermittent fevers before their anticipated attack. It is mixed with plasters that are capable of dispersing, that draw, and that are good for leprosies. 3. Infused with water or wine, it treats inflations, ringing of the ears, and purulent discharges; poured on with vinegar, it cleanses also filth. %%There are various readings of this passage for Bryges, which may be a place name. Among them there are also ponvmv. “from mountains” and vi'iomv, “from islands.” and with ass’s or pig’s fat, it treats those bitten by dogs. Compounded with turpentine, it opens up small abscesses. With figs, it is a plaster for those with edemata; smeared on with honey, it promotes sharp- sightedness; it is suitable to drink with vinegar and water for mushrooms, with water for the poisonous beetles, and with laserwort for bull’s blood. 4. It is a useful plaster for those who waste away and with cerate it abates suffering from tetanic recurvation and sprains. It is mixed beneficially also with bread for those whose tongue is paralyzed. Some bum the above by placing them in a new clay vessel on very hot coals until they become red-hot.

entry_gr: τρύγα δὲ παραλημπτέον μάλιστα μὲν τὴν ἀπὸ οἴνου παλαιοῦ Ἰταλικοῦ, εἰ δὲ μή γε, καὶ ἀπὸ ἄλλου ὁμοίου· ἡ δὲ ἀπὸ ὄξους ἐπιτέταται τῇ δυνάμει. καυσιέον δὲ ὡς ἀλκυόνιον προεξηραμμένην ἐπιμελῶς. τίνὲς δὲ ἐπ᾿ ὄστρακον καινὸν θέντες καίουσι πυρὶ δαψιλεῖ, ἕως ἂν ἐκπυρωθῇ κατὰ βάθος. ἄλλοι δὲ εἰς ἄνθρακας πεπυρωμένους ἐγκρύψαντες βῶλον ὁμοίως ποιοῦσι. σημεῖον δὲ τῆς 2 δεούσης καύσεως ἡγητέον τὸ λευκὸν ἢ ἀερόχρουν τοῦ χρώματος καὶ τὸ προσενεχθεῖσαν τῇ γλώσση οἱονεὶ φλέγειν αὐτήν. ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ ἡ ἀπὸ ὄξους καίεται. δύναμιν δὲ ἔχει καυστικὴν σφόδρα καὶ σμηκτικήν, κοτασταλτικήν τε καὶ στυπτικὴν καὶ σηπτικὴν ἄγαν καὶ ξηραντικήν. χρηστέον δὲ τῇ τρυγὶ προσφάτῳ οὔσῃ· ταχὺ γὰρ διαπνεῖται, ὅθεν οὐδὲ ἀσκέπαστον οὐδὲ χωρὶς ἄγγους αὐτὴν ἀποθετέον. πλύνεται δὲ αὕτη ὡς ἡ πομφόλυξ. ἡ δὲ ἄκαυστος στέλλει 3 οἰδήματα καθ᾿ ἑαυτὴν καὶ μετὰ μυρσίνης, καὶ κοιλίαν καὶ στόμαχον ῥευματιζόμενον καταπλασθεῖσα στέλλει, καὶ ῥοῦν γυναικεῖον κατὰ ἤτρου καὶ αἰδοίου καταπλασσομένη πραύνει, καὶ φύγεθλα ἀνέλκωτα διαφορεῖ καὶ φύματα, μαστούς τε σπαργῶντας σβέννυσιν. ἡ δὲ κεκαυμένη λεπροὺς ἀφίστησιν ὄνυχας σὺν ῥητίνῃ, καὶ μετὰ σχινίνου ἐλαίου συγχρισθεῖσα νύκτα ὅλην ξανθὰς ποιεῖ τὰς τρίχας. πλυθεῖσα δὲ μείγνυται εἰς τὰ ὀφθαλμικὰ ὡς ἡ σποδός· σμήχει δὲ οὐλὰς καὶ ἀχλῦς τὰς ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς ἡ τοιαύτη.
entry_en: 1. You must use preferably the wine lees of an old Italian wine but if unavailable you may even use those of another similar wine. Those from vinegar, however, are much too strong. You must bum them like bastard sponge, having first dried them carefully. Some place them on a new clay vessel and bum them with a big fire until reduced to ashes. Others bury a lump in red-hot coals and do the same. 2. Proof that they were burned sufficiently is their white or gray color and apparent burning of the tongue when placed on it. Vinegar lees are burned the same way also. They have strongly burning and detersive properties, also properties that are suppressive, astringent, highly putrefactive, and desiccative. You must use lees when they are fresh, for they quickly loose their strength by evaporation; it is for this reason that you must store them neither uncovered nor before putting them into a container. 3. They are washed like zinc oxide. Lees that have not been burned, reduce swellings by themselves as well as with myrtle, bind the bowel and a rheumy stomach when plastered on, assuage leucorrhea when smeared on the lower part of the abdomen and the genitalia, dissolve non-ulcerated swellings of the glands and tumors, and dry up breasts that are swollen with miUc. Burned lees remove scaly nails with pine resin and dye hair blond when anointed with oil of mastic for the whole night. Washed lees are mixed into eye medications like ashes. Lees such as these eliminate scars and misting in the eyes.

entry_gr: ἄσβεστος δὲ γίνεται μὲν οὕτως· τῶν θαλαττίων κηρύκων τὰ ὄστρακα λαβὼν πυρὶ ἔγκρυψον ἢ εἰς κλίβανον διάπυρον καθεὶς ἄφες ἐννυκτερεῦσαι. τῇ δὲ ἐχομένῃ, ἐὰν μὲν λευκότατα γένηται, ἀνελοῦ· εἰ δὲ μή, πάλιν καῖε, ἄχρις ἂν ἱκανῶς λευκανθῆ. εἶτα ἀποβάψας αὐτὰ εἰς ψυχρὸν ὕδωρ ἔμβαλε εἰς χύτραν καινὴν καὶ σκεπάσας αὐτὰ ῥάκεσιν ἐπιμελῶς ἔασον ἐνταῦθα νύκτα μίαν. πρωὶ δὲ ἀνελόμενος ἀπειληφυῖαν τὸ παντελὲς τῆς κατεργασίας ἀποτίθεσο. 2 σκευάζεται δὲ καὶ ἐκ λίθων κοχλάκων καὶ τῆς χυδαίας μαρμάρου, ἥτις καὶ προκρίνεται τῶν ἄλλων ἀσβέστων. δύναμιν δὲ ἔχει πᾶσα κοινῶς ἄσβεστος πυρωτικήν, δηκτικήν, καυστικήν, ἐσχαρωτικήν. μειγνυμένη δέ τισιν ἑτέροις ὡς στέατι ἢ ἐλαίῳ γίνεται πεπτική, μαλακτική, διασκεδαστική, κατουλωτική. ἐνεργεστέραν δὲ καὶ ταύτης ἡγητέον τὴν πρόσφατον καὶ ἄβροχον.
entry_en: 1. Unslaked lime is made this way: taking the shells of trumpet-shells, bury them into hot embers, or after placing them in a red-hot clibanos leave them alone overnight. The following day, if they should have become very white, remove them; otherwise bum them again until they become sufficiently white. Then after dipping them into cold water, place them into a new clay pot and covering them carefully with rags, leave them there for a night. In the morning, having been fully processed, take them out and store them. 2. It is also made from riverine pebbles and from common marble, which is even preferable to the other unslaked limes. 3. All unslaked limes have in common properties that heat, bite, bum, and that further the formation of eschars. But when combined with certain other ingredients, such as suet or olive oil, they can further maturation, soften, disperse, and cicatrize. That which is fresh and not wet must be considered the most effective.

entry_gr: γύψος δύναμιν ἔχει στυπτικήν, ἐμπλαστικήν, αἱμορραγίας τε καὶ ἱδρώτων ἐφεκτικήν. ποθεῖσα δὲ κτείνει τῷ κατὰ πνιγμὸν τρόπῳ.
entry_en: Gypsum has astringent, adhesive, antihemorrhagic, and antiperspirant properties. But if drunk, it kills by suffocation.

entry_gr: τέφρα κληματίνη δύναμιν ἔχει καυστικήν. σὺν ὀξυγγίῳ δὲ ἢ ἐλαίῳ καταπλασθεῖσα θλάσματά τε πλευρῶν καὶ ἄρθρων λυγίσματα καὶ συστροφὰς νεύρων ὠφελεῖ, σὺν νίτρῳ δὲ καὶ ὄξει σαρκώσεις ὀσχέου στέλλει. καταπλασθεῖσα δὲ σὺν ὄξει ἑρπετόδηκτα καὶ κυνόδηκτα ἰᾶται, ἐσχαρμωτικαῖς τε μείγνυται· καὶ πίνεται δὲ ἐξ αὐτῆς ἡ κονία πρὸς πτώματα καὶ μύκητας σὺν ἁλσὶ καὶ ὄξει.
entry_en: Ash of vine twigs has a caustic property. Plastered on with lard or with olive oil, it benefits bruised ribs, sprained joints, and twisted tendons; with soda and vinegar it reduces fleshy excrescence of the scrotum. Plastered on with vinegar it treats bites of snakes and dogs, and it is mixed with plasters that form incrustations. Its powder also is drunk with salt and vinegar for injuries due to falls and for mushrooms,

entry_gr: τοῦ δὲ ἀλκυονίου πέντε γνωστέον εἴδη ὑπάρχειν· τὸ μὲν γὰρ πυκνόν τέ ἐστι καὶ τῷ ῥυθμῷ σπογγῶδες καὶ βαρύ, ἔτι δὲ βρωμῶδες καὶ ἰχθύος ὄζον, δ᾿ δὴ πλεῖστον ἐπὶ τῶν ἠιόνων εὑρίσκεται. τὸ δὲ ἐξῆς κατὰ μὲν τὸ σχῆμα πτερυγίῳ ὀφθαλμικῷ ἢ σπόγγῳ ἔοικε, κοῦφον δέ ἐστι καὶ πολύκενον καὶ φυκώδη ἀποφορὰν ἔχον. τὸ δὲ τρίτον σκωληκοειδὲς ὑπάρχει 2 τῷ τύπῳ, καὶ τῇ χρόᾳ ἐμπόρφυρον, ὅ τινες Μιλήσιον καλοῦσι. τὸ τέταρτον δὲ ἐρίοις οἰσυπηροῖς ὅμοιον, πολύκενον, κοῦφον. τὸ δὲ πέμπτον ἔοικε μὲν κατὰ τὸ σχῆμα μύκητι, ἄνοσμον δέ ἐστι καὶ τραχὺ ἔνδοθεν, κισήρει κατά τι ἐοικός, ἔξωθεν δὲ λεῖον, δριμύ, δ᾿ πλεῖστον ἐν τῇ Προποντίδι κατὰ τὴν καλουμένην βέσβικον νῆσον γεννᾶται, δ᾿ ἐπιχωρίως ἁλὸς ἄχνην καλοῦσι. 3 τούτων τὸ μὲν πρῶτον καὶ δεύτερον εἰς σμήγματα παραλαμβάνεται γυναικῶν, καὶ πρὸς φακούς, λειχῆνάς τε καὶ λέπρας καὶ ἀλφοὺς καὶ μελανίας καὶ σπίλους τοὺς ἐπὶ τοῦ προσώπου καὶ τοῦ λοιποῦ σώματος. τὸ δὲ τρίτον εὐθετεῖ πρὸς δυσουροῦντας καὶ ἀμμώδη συλλέγοντας ἐν τῇ κύστει νεφριτικούς, πρὸς ὕδρωπας, σπλῆνας. καὲν δὲ καὶ καταχρισθὲν σὺν οἴνῳ ἀλωπεκίας θεραπεύει. 4 τὸ δὲ ὕστατον ὀδόντας λευκαίνειν δύναται· παραλαμβάνεται δὲ καὶ εἰς ἄλλα σμήγματα καὶ ψίλωθρα μισγόμενον ἁλκί. καῦσαι δὲ βουλόμενός τι τούτων εἰς ὠμὴν χύτραν ἔμβαλε καὶ περιαλείψας τὸ στόμα αὐτῆς πηλῷ δὸς εἰς κάμινον· ὅταν δὲ ὀπτηθῇ ὁ κέραμος αὐτῆς, ἀνελόμενος ἀπόθου καὶ χρῶ. πλύνεται δὲ ὡς ἡ καδμεία.
entry_en: 1. You must know that there are five kinds of alcyonia. One kind is thick, sponge-like in structure and heavy; moreover, it is malodorous %%Berendes, p. 541, n. 1, says that these are types of corals that live especially in the Red Sea and the Mediterranian. They consist of gelatine, calcium, and native salts to which they owe their use for diseases of the bladder. LSJ defines it as “bastard sponge.” and smells of fish; it is found in large quantities on beaches. The next one is similar in shape to a membrane growing from the inner comer of the eye or to a sponge; it is light, it has many hollows, and it releases a smell that is like seaweed. 2. The third is vermicular and of a purplish color; some call it Milesian. The fourth is like greasy wool, it has many holes, and it is light. And the fifth is like a mushroom in shape, it is odorless and not smooth inside, resembling somewhat pumice stone, but on the outside it is smooth and jagged; much of it grows on the Propontis, around the island called Besbicos. The locals call it salt foam. 3. The first and second of them are used in women’s cleansers, and for birthmarks, lichen-like eruptions, leprosies, dull-white leprosies, black spots, blemishes in the face and in the rest of the body. The third is good for people with difficult micturition and for patients with renal disease who collect gravelly substances in their bladder, for those with edemata, and for the spleen. Burned and smeared on with wine, it treats bald spots. 4. The last can whiten teeth; it is also used mixed with salts for other cleansers and depilatories. If you wish to bum any of them, place it into an unbaked clay pot and, after luting the opening of the pot with clay, place it in an oven. After the clay has been baked, take it out, store, and use. It is washed like calamine.

entry_gr: ὁ δὲ προσαγορευόμενος ἀδάρκης γίνεται μὲν ἐν Γαλατίᾳ, ἔστι δὲ ὥσπερ ἐπίπαγός τις ὑφαλμυρίζων, καθ᾿ ὑγρῶν καὶ τελματωδῶν τόπων ἐν ξηρασίᾳ ἐπιγινόμενος καὶ περιπηγνύμενος καλαμίοις καὶ χορταρίοις. ἔοικε δὲ τὴν χρόαν ἄνθει Ἀσκίου λίθου, τῷ δὲ ὅλῳ τύπῳ ἀλκυονίῳ τῷ μαλακῷ καὶ πολυκένῳ, καὶ ἔστιν οἱονεὶ λιμναῖον ἀλκυόνιον. εὐθετεῖ δὲ πρὸς ἐκδορὰν λεπρῶν καὶ ἐφηλίδων καὶ λειχήνων καὶ φακῶν καὶ τῶν ὁμοίων. καθόλου δέ ἐστι δριμύ, μετασυγκριτικόν, ὠφελοῦν καὶ ἰσχιάδας.
entry_en: What they call adarces occurs in Galatia; it is an incrustation, as it were, somewhat salty, forming in wet and marshy places during draught and attaching itself on reeds and grasses. Its color resembles that of the flower on Assian stone,'” but in its overall impression it resembles the alcyonion that is light and that has many hollows, and it is an alcyonion of the marshes, as it were. It is useful for the removal of leprosies, freckles, lichen-like eruptions on the skin, birthmarks, and the like. On the whole it is sharp, capable of altering the state of the pores, benefiting also hip ailments. %%This is the salt inflorescence on marsh herbs. SeeDsc. Bk.V, 124 and n. 55.

entry_gr: τῶν δὲ σπόγγων τοὺς μὲν ἄρρενας ἐκάλεσάν τινες λεπτοτρήτους καὶ πυκνοὺς ὄντας, ὧν τοὺς σκληροτάτους τράγους ὠνόμασαν, τοὺς δὲ θήλεις οἳ ἐναντίως τοῖς προειρημένοις διάκεινται. καῦσιν δὲ ἔχουσι τὴν αὐτὴν τῷ ἀλκυονίῳ. δύναται δὲ ὁ καινός τε καὶ ἀλιπὴς τραυματικός τε εἶναι καὶ οἰδήματα στέλλειν καὶ τὰ νεότρωτα κολλᾶν σὺν ὕδατι ἢ ὀξυκράτῳ, σὺν μέλιτι δὲ ἑφθῷ καὶ παλαιοὺς κόλπους παρακολλᾶν· ὁ δὲ παλαιὸς ἄχρηστος. διαστέλλουσι δὲ καὶ μεμυκότα 2 ἕλκη καὶ τύλους ἐσκελετευμένοι ἐντιθέμενοι λίνῳ, καὶ αὐτοὶ ξηροὶ παρεντιθέμενοι ὥσπερ μοτά. τὰ δὲ ῥευματικὰ ὑπόνομα καὶ χρόνια ἕλκη ἐξικμάζουσιν ἐπιτιθέμενοι ἄνικμοι καὶ κενοί, ἐπέχουσι δὲ καὶ αἱμορραγίας σὺν ἄξει. οἱ δὲ κεκαυμένοι εὔθετοι πρὸς ξηροφθαλμίας καὶ ὅπου δεῖ σμῆξαι ἢ στῦψαί τι· βέλτιον δὲ ποιοῦσι πλυθέντες εἰς τὰ ὀφθαλμικά. σὺν δὲ πίσσῃ καέντες πρὸς αἱμορραγίαν ἁρμόζουσι. 3 λευκαίνονται δὲ αὐτῶν οἱ ἁπαλώτατοι ἐν τοῖς καύμασι βρεχόμενοι τῇ ἐπὶ τῶν πετρῶν συνισταμένη ἁλὸς ἄχνῃ καὶ ἡλιαζόμενοι· ἐπιβλεπέτω δὲ τὸ μὲν κοῖλον αὐτῶν ἄνω, κάτω δὲ ἡ ἀποτομή. εἰ δὲ εἴη αἰθρία, καὶ ὑπὸ τὴν σελήνην τίθενται, βρεχόμενοι τῇ ἁλὸς ἄχνη ἢ θαλάσσῃ· γίνονται δὲ λευκότατοι οἱ τοιοῦτοι.
entry_en: 1. Some people called the sponges that have small holes and that are dense arenes^^ among which the ones that are very hard they named tragot’' and the ones that are the exact opposite of the ones just mentioned theleis.^^ Sponges are burned like bastard sponges. Sponges that are empty and devoid of any fatty substance can treat wounds, repress swellings, glue fresh wounds with water or with water and vinegar, and with boiled honey glue old hollows. But old sponges are useless. 2. When applied parched with a linen bandage, they open up closed sores and calluses, also when applied dry like pledgets. Applied dry and empty, they dry out the discharges of ulcers that contain a great deal of fluids, that spread, and that are chronic, and with vinegar they stop hemorrhages. Those that have been burned are suitable for blepharitis sicca and whenever one needs to clean or contract something. But for eye medications they are more effective if they have been washed. Burned with pitch they are suitable for hemorrhaging. 3. The ones that are very soft are bleached during the burning heat of summer. They fill them with the salt froth that settles on rocks and sun them. Make sure that their hollow part faces up and the cut side down. And if the weather is clear, they are even set out under the moon filled with salt froth or with seawater. <Such as these> do not become very white.

entry_gr: τὸ δὲ κουράλιον, ὅπερ ἔνιοι λιθόδενδρον ἐκάλεσαν, δοκεῖ μὲν εἶναι φυτὸν ἐνάλιον, στερροποιεῖσθαι δέ, ὅταν ἐκ τοῦ βυθοῦ ἑλκυσθῇ τῆς ἁλὸς ἁπτόμενον τοῦ περικεχυμένου ἡμῖν ἀέρος. εὑρίσκεται δὲ πλεῖστον ἐν τῷ κατὰ Συρακούσας ἀκρωτηρίῳ τῷ καλουμένῳ Παχύνῳ. 2 ἄριστον δέ ἐστι τὸ πυρρὸν τῇ χρόᾳ καὶ ἐμφερὲς Συρικῷ ἢ σάνδυκι κατακορεῖ, εὐθρυβές τε ὡς ἐν ἑαυτῷ καὶ ὁμαλὸν δι᾿ ὅλης τῆς συγκρίσεως, ἔτι δὲ ὀσμὴν βρυώδη καὶ φυκίοις ἐμφερῆ ἔχον, πρὸς δὲ τούτοις πολύοζον καὶ κινναμωμίζον τῷ τύπῳ τῶν θαμνίσκων. τὸ δὲ λιθῶδες τῇ συγκρίσει καὶ τῇ χρόᾳ ψωρόν, σεσηραγγωμένον τε καὶ χαῦνον φαῦλον οἰητέον εἶναι. 3 στύφει δὲ τῇ δυνάμει καὶ ψύχει ἐπιεικῶς. καταστέλλει δὲ τὰ ὑπερέχοντα καὶ οὐλὰς σμήχει τὰς ἐν ὀφθαλμῖς· πληροῖ δὲ καὶ κοιλώματα καὶ κατουλοῖ, πρὸς τε αἵματος ἀναγωγὰς ἱκανῶς ἐνεργεῖ, καὶ δυσουροῦσιν ἁρμόζει, καὶ σπλῆνα τήκει σὺν ὕδατι πινόμενον.
entry_en: 1. It seems that the coral, which some have called lithodendron,^^ is a sea plant and becomes hard when pulled from the bottom of the sea as our ambient air touches it. A great deal of it is found at the promontory called Pachynos near Syracuse. 2. Of excellent quality is that which is red in color and which resembles lead oxide or a deep red sandalwood, crumbly, as if of its %%I. e. males. I. e. he-goats. I. e. females. “Stonetree.” own accord, smooth through its entire formation, smelling like moss and seaweeds, and in addition to these characteristics, if it is ramose and like the cassia that is in the shape of small shrubs. But that which is like stone in formation, looks rough, and is hollow and porous must be presumed inferior. 3. It has properties that bind and gently cool. It reduces excrescences and it clears eye scars; it fills up hollows, it cicatrizes, it treats quite effectively blood spitting, it is suitable for people with difficult micturition, and it reduces the spleen when drunk with water.

entry_gr: καὶ τὸ καλούμενον δὲ ἀντιπαθὲς κουράλιον οἰητέον ὑπάρχειν, εἰδικὴν ἔχον διαφοράν. ἔστι δὲ τῇ μὲν χρόᾳ μέλαν, δενδρίζον δὲ καὶ αὐτὸ καὶ ὀζῶδες μᾶλλον. δύναμιν δὲ ἔχει τὴν ἴσην τῷ προειρημένῳ.
entry_en: Also that which is called antipathies must be supposed to be coral, although it has a distinct difference. It is black in color but it, too, is tree-like and quite ramose. It has the same properties as the above.

entry_gr: λίθος Φρύγιος, ᾧ ἐν Φρυγίᾳ οἱ βαφεῖς χρῶνται. ὅθεν καὶ ὠνόμασται, γεννᾶται ἐν Καππαδοκίᾳ. ἄριστος δέ ἐστιν ὁ ὠχρὸς καὶ μέσως βαρύς, οὐκ ἰσότονος τῇ συγκρίσει τοῦ χρώματος, ἔχων δὲ διαφύσεις λευκὰς ὡς ἡ καδμεία.
entry_en: 1. Phrygian stone, which the dyers in Phrygia use and from where it was named, is formed in Cappadocia. Best is that which is pale and moderately heavy, not uniformly colored, and having white crevices just like calamine. 2. It is burned this way: after wetting it with the best possible wine, bury it in red-hot coals and keep fanning it. When it has changed color becoming more orange-tawny, take it out, quench it with the same kind of wine, and repeat the process, burying it again in the coals. Then bum it a third time, taking care that it does not break nor becomes sooty. 3. Unfired as well as fired it has properties that are highly astringent; additionally, they are detersive, escharotic, curative of bums with cerate, and mildly putrefactive. It is washed like calamine.

entry_gr: Ἄσσιον δὲ λίθον παραλημπτέον τὸν κισηροειδῆ τὴν χρόαν, χαῦνόν τε καὶ κοῦφον, ἔτι δὲ εὐθρυβῆ καὶ διαφύσεις μηλίνας ἔχοντα διὰ βάθους. τὸ δὲ ἄν θος αὐτοῦ ἐστιν ἡ ἐφιζάνουσα ἁλμυρὶς τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ τῶν λίθων, τῇ μὲν συστάσει λεπτή, τῇ δὲ χρόᾳ τὸ μέν τι λευκόν ἐστι, τὸ δέ τι ἔοικε κισήρει, ἐπὶ τὸ μήλινον τετραμμένον, προσαγόμενόν τε τῇ γλώττῃ δάκνει ποσῶς. 2 δύναμιν δὲ ἔχει ἑκάτερον σηπτικὴν ἡσυχῆ καὶ διαφορητικὴν φυμάτων τερεβινθίνῃ ἀναλαμβανόμενον ῥητίνῃ ἢ πίσσῃ. εὐτονώτερον δὲ τὸ ἄνθος ἡγητέον· ἐκ περισσοῦ δὲ τοῦτο ξηραινόμενον τὰ παλαιὰ καὶ δυσκατούλωτα ἕλκη ἰᾶται, καταστέλλει δὲ τὰ ὑπερσαρκοῦντα καὶ μύκησιν ἅμοια καὶ θηριώδη. πληροῖ δὲ καὶ τὰ κοῖλα τῶν ἑλκῶν καὶ ἀνακαθαίρει σὺν μέλιτι, καὶ τὰ νεμόμενα δὲ ἵστησι μιγὲν κηρωτῇ. 3 ποιεῖ καὶ ποδαγρικοῖς ἐν καταπλάσμασι μετ᾿ ἐρεγμοῦ, καὶ σπληνικοῖς μετ᾿ ὄξους καὶ ἀσβέστου, ἐκλειχόμενόν τε [τὸ ἄνθος] μετὰ μέλιτος φθισικοὺς ὠφελεῖ, κατασκευάζονται δὲ καὶ πύελοι ἐκ τοῦ λίθου, εἰς ἃς οἱ ποδαγρικοὶ τοὺς πόδας ἐντιθέντες ὠφελοῦνται, καὶ σοροὶ σαρκοφάγοι γίνονται. ἰσχναίνει καὶ τὰ πολύσαρκα καὶ παχέα σώματα καταπασσόμενον ἀντὶ νίτρου ἐν βαλανείῳ. ἐὰν δέ τις πλῦναι θέλῃ τὰ προειρημένα, πλυνέτω ὡς τὴν καδμείαν.
entry_en: 1. You must use Assian stone of a pumice color, porous and light, crumbly, and with deep, quince-yellow crevices. Its flower is the salt that rises on the surface of the stones; it is fine in structure, some is %%54 A kind of aluminous pumice-stone. white in color, some resembles somewhat the color of pumice tending towards quince-yellow, and it bites slightly when placed on the tongue. 2. Each has properties that are mildly putrefactive and dispersive of growths when taken with turpentine or pitch. But the flower must be regarded as the stronger of the two. The latter, when it has dried, treats marvelously well sores that are old and hard to cicatrize and reduces sores that are overgrown, mushroom-like, and malignant. With honey it also fills up the concavities of ulcers and cleanses them, and with cerate it controls spreading ulcers. 3. Used in plasters with bruised com, <it is good> for the gouty, with vinegar and unslaked lime, for people with spleen disease, and when sucked with honey it benefits the tuberculars. From this stone they also make tubs that help gout sufferers who place their feet into them, and they make flesh-consuming coffins.<Its flower> reduces fleshy as well as obese bodies when applied as a plastered in the bath, instead of soda. If one wishes to wash the above, he should wash them like calamine.

entry_gr: πυρίτης λίθος εἰδός ἐστι λίθου, ἀφ᾿ οὗ ὁ χαλκὸς μεταλλεύεται. λημπτέον μέντοι τὸν χαλκοειδῆ εὐχερῶς τε σπινθῆρας ἀφιέντα. καυστέον δὲ τῷ τρόπῳ τούτῳ· μέλιτι δεύσας αὐτὸν ἔνθες εἰς ἀνθρακιὰν μαλακὴν καὶ ῥίπιζε συνεχῶς, ἕως ἂν τὴν χρόαν κιρρὸς γένηται. ἔνιοι δὲ εἰς πολλοὺς καὶ πεπυρωμένους ἄνθρακας ἀποτίθενται ἱκανῶς βεβρεγμένον τῷ μέλιτι τὸν λίθον· ὅταν δὲ μέλλῃ τρέπεσθαι ἐπὶ τὸ κιρρότερον, 2 ἀναιροῦνται, καὶ ἀποφυσήσαντες τὴν σποδὸν πάλιν καίουσι διάβροχον, ἕως ἂν ψαθυρώτατος γένηται ὁμαλῶς· πολλάκις γὰρ μόνον ἐπικαίεται τὴν ἐπιφάνειαν. οὕτω δὲ ἀποκαύσαντες καὶ ξηράναντες ἀποτίθενται. ἐὰν δὲ πεπλυμένου χρεία ὑπάρχῃ. πλυτέον ὡς τὴν καδμείαν. δύναμιν δὲ ἔχει κεκαυμένος τε καὶ ὠμὸς θερμαντικήν τε 3 καὶ σμηκτικὴν καὶ ἀποκαθαρτικὴν τῶν ἐπισκοτούντων ταῖς κόραις, διαφορητικήν τε καὶ πεπαντικὴν σκληρωμάτων ἀναλημφθεὶς ῥητίνῃ· καταστέλλει δὲ καὶ τὰ ὑπερσαρκοῦντα μετὰ ποσῆς θερμασίας καὶ στύψεως. καλοῦσι δὲ ἔν ιοι τὸν οὕτω καέντα διφρνγές.
entry_en: 1. Copper pyrites is a type of stone from which copper is mined. You must choose that which is copper-colored and which emits sparks readily. You must bum it this way: after coating it with honey, place it on gently burning coals and fan it continuously until it becomes orange-tawny in color. But some people, after moistening it well with honey, bury it among many very hot coals. 2. When it is about to become more orange-tawny, remove it and, after blowing off the ash again, bum it moistened until it becomes uniformly quite brittle. For it is often burned only on the surface. After burning it then this way and drying it, they store it. And if it is needed washed, it must be washed like calamine. %%Celsus, 4,31,7, Pliny, N. H., 2.211, 36.131 also mention this stone for its remarkable ability to eat the flesh of corpses laid in sarcophagi constructed from it and to allay pain. It gets its name from Assos, a town of the Troad, where excellent Assian stones were quarried. 3. Both burned and not burned it is capable of warming, purging, cleansing the elements that cast a shadow over the pupils of the eyes, and of dissolving and softening indurations when compounded with pine resin. It also reduces overgrown flesh with some degree of warmth and astringency. Some call the one that was burned this way diphryges.^^

entry_gr: αἱματίτης δὲ λίθος ἄριστός ἐστιν ὁ εὐθρυβὴς μὲν ὡς ἐν ἑαυτῷ, σκληρὸς δὲ καὶ κατακορὴς ὁμαλῶς, ἀνεπίμικτος ῥυπαρίας τινὸς ἢ διαζωμάτων. δύναμιν δὲ ἔχει στυπτικὴν καὶ θερμαντικὴν ποσῶς καὶ λεπτυντικὴν καὶ σμηκτικὴν οὐλῶν τῶν ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς καὶ τραχωμάτων σὺν μέλιτι, σὺν δὲ γάλακτι γυναικείῳ πρὸς ὀφθαλμίας καὶ ῥήξεις καὶ ὑφαίμους ὀφθαλμούς. 2 πίνεται δὲ σὺν οἴνῳ πρὸς δυσουρίας καὶ ῥοικάς, καὶ πρὸς αἵματος πτύσιν σὺν χυλῷ ῥόας· γίνεται δὲ καὶ κολλούρια καὶ ἀκόνια ἐξ αὐτοῦ πρὸς τὰ ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς πάθη ἐπιτήδεια. καίεται δὲ ἐμφερῶς τῷ Φρυγίῳ λίθῳ τοῦ οἴνου περιῃρημένου· μέτρον δὲ ἔστω τῆς καύσεως τὸ γενέσθαι αὐτὸν μέσως κοῦφον καὶ πεπομφολυγωμένον. 3 δολοῦσι δέ τινες τὸν προειρημένον οὕτω· λαβόντες βῶλον σχιστοῦ λίθου πυκνόν τε καὶ στρογγύλον — τοιαῦται δέ εἰσιν αὐτοῦ αἱ λεγόμεναι ῥίζαι — είς κεραμεᾶν γάστραν σποδιὰν ἔχουσαν θερμὴν ἐγκρύπτουσιν, εἶτα διαλιπόντες μικρὸν ἀναιροῦνται καὶ ἐπ᾿ ἀκόνης τρίβουσι δοκιμάζοντες, εἰ τὴν αἱματίτου χρόαν ἀπείληφε. 4 κἂν μὲν οὕτως ἔχῃ, ἀποτίθενται, εἰ δὲ μή, πάλιν ἐγκρύπτουσι, συνεχῶς ἐφορῶντες καὶ δοκιμάζοντες· ἀφεθεὶς γὰρ ἐπὶ πολὺ ἐν τῇ σποδιᾷ μεταβάλλει τῷ χρώματι, ἔπειτα καὶ διαχεῖται. ἀπελέγχεται δὲ ὁ κεκακοτεχνημένος πρῶτον μὲν ταῖς διαφύσεσιν· ὁ μὲν γὰρ ἐπʼ εὐθείας εἰς κτηδόνας ἀποκλᾶται ὁ δὲ αἱματίτης οὐχ οὕτως ἔχει· εῖτα καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς χρόας· ὁ μὲν γὰρ εὐανθὲς ἀνίησιν ὁ 5 δὲ αἱματίτης βαθύτερον καὶ τῷ κινναβάρει ἐοικός. εὑρίσκεται δὲ ἐν τῇ Σινωπικῇ μίλτῳ, καὶ ἐκ τῆς μαγνήτιδος δὲ πέτρας καιοκένης ἐφ᾿ ἱκανὸν κατασκευάζεται, αἱματίτης δὲ αὐτοφυὴς ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ μεταλλεύεται.
entry_en: 1. Hematite is of excellent quality when it breaks easily as if of its own accord and when it is hard, uniformly strong, and free of any dirt or veins. It has properties that are astringent, that warm somewhat, that thin, and, with honey, that wipe off scars and roughnesses in the eyes. With woman’s milk it is good for ophthalmia, for rents,” and for bloodshot eyes. 2. It is drunk with wine for difficult micturition and for leucorrhea and with the juice of pomegranate for blood spitting. They make from it both salves and medications suitable for eye diseases. It is burned like Phrygian stone but without the wine. Let the standard for burning it be that it becomes moderately light and full of bubbles. 3. Some fake the above this way: taking a lump of talc that is dense and round — such are its so-called ‘roots’ — bury it in a clay pot that contains hot ashes then after a while they remove it and rub it against a whetstone testing whether it acquired the color of hematite. 4. And if it has that color, they store it, otherwise they again bury it, constantly checking and testing it: for if it is left alone for a long time in the ashes, it changes color and it even disintegrates. The counterfeit is refuted first from its divisions. For it breaks off in layers right away, but hematite does not break so. 5. Then it is refuted also from its color because the counterfeit has a fresh-looking color, but hematite is of a deeper color and it resembles cinnabar. It is found in Sinopic red earth, it is also made from magnet that was burned for a while, but natural hematite is mined in Egypt. %%“Twice roasted.” Probably, in the eyes.

entry_gr: σχιστὸς δὲ λίθος γεννᾶται μὲν ἐν τῇ καθ᾿ ἐσπέραν Ἰβηρίᾳ, ἄριστος δὲ εἶναι δοκεῖ ὁ παρακροκίζων τῇ χρόᾳ, εὐθρυβής τε καὶ εὔσχιστος ὡς ἐν ἑαυτῷ· ἔοικε δὲ τῆς συνθέσεως ἕνεκεν καὶ ἀλληλουχίας τῶν κτηδόνων αὐτοῦ ἀμμωνιακῷ ἁλί. δύναμιν δὲ τὴν αὐτὴν τῷ αἱματίτῃ εἰσφέρεται, τῇ εὐτονίᾳ 2 μόνον λειπόμενος αὐτοῦ. πληροῖ δὲ καὶ κοιλώματα γυναικείῳ διεθεὶς γάλακτι, καὶ πρὸς ῥήξεις καὶ προπτώσεις, ἔτι δὲ τραχύτητας βλεφάρων καὶ σταφυλώματα λίαν ἐνεργεῖ.
entry_en: 1. Talc is formed in the western part of Spain and it seems to be excellent when it is somewhat saffron-colored and breakable and when it splits easily, as if of its own accord. Because of its composition and of the close texture of its layers it resembles rock salt. 2. It has the same properties as hematite, falling short of it only in strength. It fills up hollows when diluted with woman’s milk and it is very effective both for rents and for prolapses of the eyes, also for roughness of the eyelids and for defects inside the cornea.

entry_gr: τοῦ δὲ γαγάτου προκριτέον τὸν ταχέως ἐξαπτόμενον καὶ ἀσφαλτίζοντα ἐν τῇ ὀσμῇ· μέλας δὲ κοινῶς ὑπάρχει καὶ αὐχμηρός, ἔτι δὲ πλακώδης καὶ κοῦφος ἄγαν. δύναμιν δὲ ἔχει μαλακτικὴν καὶ διαφορητικήν· ἔστι δὲ καὶ ἐπιλημπτικῶν ἔλεγχος ὑποθυμιαθείς, καὶ ὑστερικὰς ἀνακαλεῖται. 2 διώκει δὲ καὶ ἑρπετὰ θυμιαθείς, καὶ ποδαγρικαῖς μείγνυται δυνάμεσι. γεννᾶται δὲ ἐν Λυκίᾳ εὑρισκόμενος κατά τινος ποταμοῦ ἔκρυσιν εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν ἐκχεομένου· καλεῖται δὲ ὁ τόπος Γάγαι.
entry_en: 1. You must choose lignite that catches fire quickly and that smells hke asphalt. It is generally black and dry and it is flaky and very light. It has softening and dissolving properties; it is a test for epileptics when burned as to produce smoke from below, and it revives women in a state of uterine suffocation. 2. It drives away serpents when burned as to produce smoke and it is combined with medications that are good for the gouty. It occurs in Lycia, being found along the issue of a certain river that empties itself into the sea. The place is called Gagai.

entry_gr: ὁ δὲ λεγόμενος Θρᾳκίας γεννᾶται μὲν κατὰ Σιντίαν ἐν ποταμῷ τῷ λεγομένῳ Πόντῳ. δύναται δὲ τὰ αὐτὰ τῷ γαγάτῃ. ἱστορεῖται δὲ ἐκκαίεσθαι μὲν αὐτὸν ὕδατι, σβέννυσθαι δὲ ὑπ᾿ ἐλαίου, ὅπερ καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς ἀσφάλτου γίνεται
entry_en: The stone called Thracian is formed in Sintia, in the river called Pontos. It can do the same things as lignite. It is reported that it is set on fire with water and that it is quenched with oil, something that happens also to asphalt.

entry_gr: τοῦ δὲ μαγνήτου λίθου ἄριστός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν σίδηρον εὐχερῶς ἕλκων καὶ τὴν χρόαν κυανίζων, πυκνός τε καὶ οὐκ ἄγαν βαρύς. δύναμιν δὲ ἔχει πάχους ἀγωγὸν διδόμενος μετὰ μελικράτου τριωβόλου βάρος. ἔνιοι δὲ τοῦτον καίοντες ἀντὶ αἱματίτου πιπράσκουσιν.
entry_en: The best magnet attracts iron easily, is bluish in color, dense, and not too heavy. It has a property that drives out thick masses when given in the amount of one triobolon with hydromel. Some people bum it and sell it as hematite. %%58 Conjecture in LSJ.

entry_gr: ὁ δὲ Ἀραβικὸς λεγόμενος λίθος ἔοικεν ἐλέφαντι ἀσπίλῳ. οὗτος λεῖος καταπλασθεὶς αἱμορροίδας ἀποξηραίνει, καεὶς δὲ ὀδόντων σμῆγμα γίνεται.
entry_en: The stone called Arabian resembles flawless ivory. This stone dries up hemorrhoids when applied ground up and after it is burned it becomes dentifrice.

entry_gr: ὁ δὲ γαλακτίτης ὠνόμασται ἀπὸ τοῦ γαλακτῶδες ἀνιέναι· ἔστι μέντοι ἄλλως ἔντεφρος τὴν χρόαν, γλυκύς τε πρὸς τὴν γεῦσιν. ἁρμόζει δὲ πρὸς ἀφθαλμῶν ῥεύματα καὶ ἕλκη ἐγχριόμενος. δεῖ δὲ τρίψαντας αὐιὸν ἐν ὕδατι ἀποτίθεσθαι ἐν πυξίδι μολυβδίνῃ διὰ τὸ περὶ αὐτὸν κολλῶδες.
entry_en: Milkstone was named from the milk-like solute it releases. Otherwise it is really ash-colored and sweet in taste. It is suitable to smear on for running eyes and for eye sores. After reducing it into powder you must store it in water, in a leaden box, for the starchy element surrounding it.

entry_gr: ὁ δὲ μελιτίτης κατὰ πάντα ἔοικε τῷ γαλακτίτῃ, διαφέρων ἐν τῷ γλυκύτατον ἀνιέναι τὸν χυλόν. ποιεῖ δὲ πρὸς ἃ καὶ ὁ γαλακτίτης.
entry_en: Honeystone resembles milkstone in every respect, differing only in that the juice it releases is very sweet. It is good for all the things that milkstone is also good.

entry_gr: λίθος μόροχθος, δν ἔνιοι γαλαξίαν ἢ λευκογραφίδα ἐκάλεσαν, ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ γεννᾶται, ᾧ καὶ οἱ ὀθονιοποιοὶ πρὸς λεύκανσιν τῶν ὀθονίων χρῶνται, μαλακῷ καὶ εὐανέτῳ ὄντι. δοκεῖ δὲ παρεμπλάσσειν, ἁρμόζων ἐπὶ αἱμοπτυικῶν καὶ κοιλιακῶν καὶ κύστεως ἀλγημάτων σὺν ὕδατι πινόμενος, καὶ ῥοικαῖς ὁμοίως καὶ ἐν προσθέτῳ, εἴς τε τὰ μαλακὰ ὀφθαλμικὰ μείγνυται· πληροῖ γὰρ κοιλώματα καὶ ῥεύματα ἵστησι. σὺν δὲ κηρωτῇ ἀναλημφθεὶς τὰ τρυφερά τῶν ἑλκῶν ἀπουλοῖ.
entry_en: Pipe clay, which some people have called galaxias or leucographis, is produced in Egypt. The weavers of linen use it to whiten linens, being soft and easy to dissolve. It is thought to stop the pores. It is suitable for people who spit blood, for the colicky, for bladder ailments when drunk with water, and similarly for women who suffer from discharges and in a pessary. It is also mixed into soft eye medications. For it does fill up hollows and it stems discharges. Compounded with cerate, it cicatrizes the tender parts of ulcers.

entry_gr: λίθος ἀλαβαστρίτης ὁ καλούμενος ὄνυξ ἀναλημφθεὶς κεκαυμένος ῥητίνη ἢ πίσσῃ διαφορεῖ σκληρίας, στομάχου δὲ ἀλγήματα μετὰ κηρωτῆς παρηγορεῖ· στέλλει δὲ καὶ οὖλα.
entry_en: The alabaster called onyx, compounded with pine resin or pitch after'it has been burned, dissolves indurations, and with cerate it assuages stomach pains. It also tightens the gums.

entry_gr: λίθος ὁ καλούμενος θυίτης γεννᾶται μὲν ἐν τῇ Αἰθιοπίᾳ, ἔστι δὲ ὑπόχλωρος, ἰασπίζων, ἐν δὲ τῷ ἀνίεσθαι γαλακτώδης φαινόμενος, ἀναδάκνων σφοδρῶς. δύναμιν δὲ ἔχει ἀποκαθαρτικὴν τῶν ταῖς κόραις ἐπιδκοτούντὸν.
entry_en: The stone called thyites is produced in Ethiopia. It is greenish-yellow, it is jasper-like, it appears milky when broken, and it bites a great deal. It has a property that cleanses the elements that cast a shadow over the pupils of the eyes.

entry_gr: ὁ δὲ Ἰουδαικὸς λίθος γεννᾶται μὲν ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ, τῷ σχήματι βαλανοειδής, λευκός, εὔρυθμος ἱκανῶς, ἔχων γραμμὰς παραλλήλους ὡς ἀπὸ τόρνου, ἀνιέμενος δέ ἐστιν ἄποιος ἐν τῇ γεύσει. δύναται δὲ ἐρεβινθιαῖον μέγεθος διεθὲν ὡς κολλούριον ἐπ᾿ ἀκόνης σὺν ὕδατος θερμοῦ κυάθοις τρισὶ καὶ ποθὲν δυσουρίαις βοηθεῖν καὶ τοὺς ἐν κύστει λίθους θρύπτειν.
entry_en: Judaic stone is produced in Judea. It is shaped like an acorn; it is white, quite smooth, with parallel lines as if made on a turning lathe, and tasteless when dissolved. An amount in size like a bean, dissolved like a little pill on a whetstone with three cyathoi of hot water and drunk, can help for difficult micturition and break bladder stones.

entry_gr: λίθος ἀμίαν τος γεννᾶται μὲν ἐν Κύπρῳ, στυπτηρίᾳ σχιστῇ ἐοικώς, δν ἐργαζόμενοι οἱ τῆδε ἄνθρωποι ὑφάσματα ποιοῦσιν ἐξ αὐτοῦ, ὄντος ἱμαντώδους, πρὸς θέαν. ἐμβληθεὶς δὲ εἰς πῦρ φλογοῦται μέν, λαμπρότερος δὲ ἐξέρχεται μὴ κατακαιόμενος.
entry_en: Asbestos is produced in Cyprus, it resembles cleft alum, and, because it is fibrous, the people who work with it there make fabrics from it for shows. Thrown into a fire, while it does flare up, it comes out brighter, not burned.

entry_gr: λίθος σάπφειρος δοκεῖ ὠφελεῖν σκορπιοπλήκτους πινόμενος· πίνεται δὲ καὶ πρὸς τὰς ἐντὸς ἑλκώσεις, καὶ τὰς ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς ὑπεροχὸς καὶ σταφυλώματα καὶ φλυκταίνας στέλλει, καὶ τὰς ῥήξεις τῶν ὑμένων συνάγει.
entry_en: Lapis lazuli seems to help people stung by scorpions when drunk. It is drunk for internal ulcerations and it shrinks excrescences, defects inside the cornea and pustules on the eyes, and it joins together the rents of their membranes.

entry_gr: λίθος Μεμφίτης εὑρίσκεται ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ κατὰ Μέμφιν, ἔχων ψήφων μέγεθος, λιπαρὸς καὶ ποικίλος. οὗτος ἱστορεῖται καταχρισθεὶς λεῖος ἐπὶ τῶν μελλόντων τέμνεσθαι καίεσθαι τόπων ἀκίνδυνον ἀναισθησίαν ἐπιφέρειν.
entry_en: Memphitic stone is found in Egypt, around Memphis. It is of the size of a pebble, shiny, and pied. Ground up and smeared on areas about to be operated or cauterized, this stone is reported to induce harmless anesthesia. %%“Turquoise,” John Goodyer, The Greek herbal of Dioscorides, p. 654. No identification in LSJ. Identified as retinasphaltum in John Goodyer, op. cit. p. 655 and described by Charles Hatchett, Trans. Linn. Soc. iv, p. 140.

entry_gr: λίθος σεληνίτης, ὅν τινες ἀφροσέληνον ἐκάλεσαν διὰ τὸ εὑρίσκεσθαι αὐτὸν νυκτὸς ἐν τῇ τῆς σελήνης παραυξήσει, γεννᾶται ἐν Ἀραβίᾳ, λευκός, διαυγής, κοῦφος. τοῦτον ἀποξύοντες διδόασι πόμα ἐπιλημπτικοῖς. καὶ ἀντὶ φυλακτηρίου δὲ περιάμματι αὐτῷ αἱ γυναῖκες χρῶνται. δοκεῖ δὲ καὶ δένδρεσι προστεθεὶς καρπογόνος εἶναι.
entry_en: Selenite, which some people have called aphroselenos^^ because it is found at night when the moon waxes, occurs in Arabia. It is white, transparent, and light. It is given as a drink to epileptics and women use it as a protective amulet. It also seems to make trees fruitful when attached to them.

entry_gr: λίθος ἴασπις· ὁ μέν τίς ἐστι σμαραγδίζων, ὁ δὲ κρυσταλλοειδής, ἐοικώς φλέγματι, ὁ δὲ ἀερίζων, ὁ δὲ καπνίας ὡσπερεὶ κεκαπνισμένος, ὁ δέ τις [καὶ] διαφύσεις ἔχων διαλεύκους καὶ ἀποστιλβούσας, ἄστριος καλούμενος, ὁ δέ τις τερεβινθίζων λέγεται, καλλαίνῳ χρώματι προσεοικώς. δοκοῦσι δὲ πάντες εἶναι φυλακτήρια περίαπτα καὶ ὠκυτόκια μηρῷ περιαπτόμενα.
entry_en: There is a jasper which is emerald green, another like crystal, resembling phlegm, another light blue,26^ another smoky, as if it were blackened with smoke, one which has cracks that are quite white and shining and which is called astrios, and there is one called terebinthizon, resembling turquoise in color. All seem to guard against evil when hung on a person and to promote a speedy birth when tied around the thigh.

entry_gr: λίθος ὀφίτης· ὁ μέν τίς ἐστι στιβαρός, μέλας, ὁ δὲ σποδοειδὴς τὴν χρόαν καὶ κατεστιγμένος, ὁ δέ τις γραμμὰς ἔχων λευκάς. πάντες δὲ εὐχρηστοῦσι περιαπτόμενοι ἐπὶ ἐχεοδήκτων καὶ ἐπὶ κεφαλαλγούντων. ὁ δὲ τὰς γραμμὰς ἔχων ἰδίως ἱστορεῖται ληθάργῳ καὶ κεφαλαλγίαις βοηθεῖν.
entry_en: There is a scrprntine that is sturdy and black, another ash-colored and spotted, and another that has white lines. All are useful when tied on people stung by vipers or on those who have headaches. The one that has the lines is reported to be particularly helpful for lethargic fever and headaches.

entry_gr: λίθοι οἱ ἐν τοῖς σπόγγοις εὑρισκόμενοι σὺν οἴνῳ ποθέντες τοὺς ἐν κύστει λίθους θρύπτουσιν.
entry_en: When drunk with wine, the stones found in sponges break stones in the bladder.

entry_gr: ἡ δὲ λιθοκόλλα, μεῖγμα οὖσα μαρμάρου ἢ λίθου Παρίου καὶ ταυροκόλλης, δύναται διὰ μηλωτίδος πεπυρωμένης τρίχας ἀνακολλᾶν τὰς ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς.
entry_en: Stone glue, which is a mixture of marble or of Parian stone and bull’s hide glue, when used with a very hot probe, can glue back eyelashes.

entry_gr: λίθος ὀστρακίτης ὅμοιός ἐστιν ὀστράκῳ, εὔσχιστος καὶ πλακώδης, ᾧ χρῶνται ἀντὶ κισήρεως πρὸς τριχῶν ἄρσιν αἱ γυναῖκες. ἴσχει δὲ καὶ καταμήνια πινόμενος σὺν οἴνῳ δραχμῆς μιᾶς πλῆθος, δυεῖν δὲ βάρος ἐὰν πίνῃ τις ἐπὶ ἡμέρας δ΄ μετὰ τὴν ἄφεδρον, ἀσυλλημψίαν ποιεῖ. σὺν μέλιτι δὲ ἐπιτιθέμενος μαστοὺς φλεγμαίνοντας παρηγορεῖ καὶ νομὰς ἵστησιν.
entry_en: Clay stone is like a shell, it is easy to split, and it is flaky. Women use it instead of pumice for hair removal. An amount of one drachma %%“Moon-foam.” Or perhaps, “grey” or “cloudy.” drunk with wine stops the menstrual period and a weight of two drachmai drunk for four days following menstruation causes barrenness. Applied with honey on inflamed breasts, it soothes them and it also stops spreading ulcers.

entry_gr: σμύρις λίθος ἐστίν, ᾗ τὰς ψήφους οἱ λιθογλύφοι σμήχουσι, χρησίμη εἰς σηπτὰς καὶ καυστικάς, καὶ πρὸς οὔλων πλαδώντων καὶ ὀδόντων σμῆξιν.
entry_en: Emery is a stone that lapidaries use to clean their gems. It is useful for putrefactive and caustic medications, for flaccid gums, and as a dentifrice.

entry_gr: ἄμμος ἡ παρὰ τοῖς αἰγιαλοῖς πυρωθεῖσα ὑπὸ τοῦ ἡλίου ἐξικμάζει τὰ ὑδερώδη σώματα περιχωννύμενα δίχα κεφαλῆς· φώγνυται δὲ καὶ εἰς τὰς ξηρὰς πυρίας ἀντὶ κέγχρου ἢ ἁλῶν.
entry_en: Sand that has been heated by the sun at the beach draws out moisture from edematose bodies when heaped over them up to the head. It is also roasted instead of millet or salts for dry fomentations.

entry_gr: ἀκόνης Ναξίας τὸ ἀπότριμμα τοῦ πρὸς αὐτὴν ἀκονηθέντος σιδήρου ἐπιχρισθὲν ἀλωπεκίας τριχοῖ καὶ μαστοὺς παρθένων κωλύει αὔξεσθαι. ποθὲν δὲ μετ᾿ ὄξους σπλῆνα τήκει καὶ ἐπιλημπτικοὺς ὠφελεῖ.
entry_en: The powder from Naxian whetstone produced when iron is honed against it causes hair to grow on bald spots and prevents maiden breasts from growing big when smeared on them. It reduces the spleen and it benefits epileptics when drunk with vinegar.

entry_gr: λίθος γεώδης στύφει, ξηραίνει, ἀποκαθαίρει τὰ ἐπισκοτοῦντα ταῖς κόραις τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν. καταχρισθεὶς δὲ μεθ᾿ ὕδατος μαστῶν καὶ ὄρχεων παύει φλεγμονάς.
entry_en: The earth-like stone binds, dries, and cleanses the elements that cast a shadow over the pupils of the eyes. Smeared on with water, it stops inflammations of the breasts and testicles.

entry_gr: γῆ δὲ πᾶσα ἡ πίπτουσα εἰς ἰατρικὴν χρῆσιν τὴν μὲν ἀνωτάτω δύναμιν ἔχει ψύχουσαν καὶ παρεμπλάσσουσαν, κατ᾿ εἶδος δὲ διαφέρει ἄλλης εἰς ἄλλα μετά τινος σκευασίας χρησιμευούσης.
entry_en: All earths employed in medicine have properties that cool to the utmost and stop the pores. They differ from each other in kind and they are used, after some preparation, for different purposes.

entry_gr: τῆς μὲν οὖν Ἑρετριάδος γῆς ἡ μέν τίς ἐστι λευκὴ ἐπιτεταμένως ἡ δὲ σποδοειδής· ἀρίστη δὲ ὑπάρχει ἡ τῇ χρόᾳ σποδίζουσα καὶ μαλακὴ ἄγαν, πρός τε χαλκώματα ἑλκυσθεῖσα γραμμὴν ἰώδη ἀποφερομένη. πλύνεται δὲ ὡς ψιμύθιον, ἢ οὕτως· λεάνας αὐτῆς ὅσον ἂν θέλῃς κατ᾿ ἰδίαν τε καὶ σὺν ὕδατι ἔασον καταστῆναι. εἶτα τὸ μὲν ὑγρὸν ἀπήθησον, τὴν δὲ γῆν ἐν ἡλίῳ ξηράνας πάλιν τρῖβε ἐπὶ ἡμέραν, ἐπιδοὺς ὕδωρ, ἐσπέρας δὲ ἐάσας ὑποστῆναι. περὶ τὸν ἄρθρον ἀπήθησον καὶ λεάνας ἐν ἡλίῳ ἀνάπλασσε τροχίσκους, εἰ δυνατὸν εἴη. ἐὰν δὲ ὠπτημένης χρεία ὑπάρῃ, 2 λαβὼν ἐρεβινθιαῖα μεγέθη τῆς γῆς δὸς εἰς ἀγγεῖον κεραμεοῦν κατατετρημένον, πωμάσας τε τὸ στόμα ἐπιμελῶς ἔνθες εἰς διαπύρους ἄνθρακας καὶ ῥίπιζε συνεχῶς· ὅταν δὲ σποδῷ αἰθαλώδει μᾶλλον ἐμφερὴς γένηται τὴν χρόαν, ἀνελόμενος ἀπόθου. δύναμιν δὲ ἔχει στυπτικὴν καὶ ψυκτικήν, κούφως μαλακτικήν, κοιλωμάτων πληρωτικήν, ἐναίμων κολλητικήν.
entry_en: 1. One kind of Eretrian earth is exceedingly white, another ashen. The best is ash-colored, very soft, and when drawn against brazen objects, it leaves behind a rust-colored line. It is washed like white lead or as follows; after triturating as much of it as you may wish by itself as well as with water, let it settle. Then strain out the liquid, and after drying the earth in the sun, pound it again during the day, adding water, and, letting it settle during the night, around dawn strain, and, pounding it in the sun, shape small troches if you can. 2. But if there is need for it to be cooked, take bean-size pieces of this earth, place in a perforated earthen vessel, seal its mouth carefully, place on red-hot coals, and fan continuously. When it becomes somewhat like sooty ash, remove and store. It has astringent and cooling properties, gently softening, filling hollows, and gluing together bleeding wounds.

entry_gr: τῆς δὲ Σαμίας γῆς τὴν ἄγαν λευκὴν προκριτέον καὶ ἐλαφρὰν καὶ ἐν τῷ θιγεῖν τῇ γλώσση κρατουμένην ἐχεκόλλως, ἔτι δὲ εὔχυτον καὶ μαλακὴν καὶ εὐθρυβῆ, οἵα ἐστίν, ἥν τινες κολλούριον καλοῦσιν. ἔστι δὲ αὐτῆς δύο εἴδη· τό τε προειρημένον καὶ ὁ καλούμενος ἀστήρ, πλακώδης ὢν καὶ πυκνὸς ὡς ἀκόνη. 2 δύναμιν δὲ ἔχει καὶ καῦσιν καὶ πλύσιν ἐμφερῆ Ἐρετριάδι. ἰστησι καὶ αἵματος ἀναγωγήν, καὶ ῥοικαῖς δίδοται γυναιξὶ σὺν βαλαυστίῳ, καὶ ὄρχεων καὶ μαστῶν φλεγμονὰς καταχριομένη σὺν ὕδατι καὶ ῥοδίνῳ στέλλει καὶ ἱδρῶτας, καὶ θηριοδήκτοις καὶ θανασίμοις ἀρήγει πινομένη σὺν οἴνῳ.
entry_en: 1. You must choose Samian earth that is very white, light, and when it touches the tongue it sticks to it like glue; also, you must choose it easily soluble, soft, and crumbly. Such is the Samian earth which some call collourion. There are two kinds of it: the one just mentioned and the one called aster, which is crusty and dense like whetstone. 2. Its properties, burning, and washing are similar to those of Eretrian earth. It stops blood spitting, it is given with flower of wild pomegranate to women who suffer from discharges, it represses inflammations of the testicles, of the breasts, and sweats when rubbed on with water and unguent of roses, and it helps those bitten by wild animals and for poisons when drunk with wine.

entry_gr: εὑρίσκεται δέ τις ἐν τῇ Σαμίᾳ γῇ λίθος, ᾧ οἱ χρυσοχόοι χρῶνται πρὸς τὸ λεαίνειν καὶ στιλβοῦν· διαφέρει δὲ ὁ λευκὸς καὶ στιβαρός. δύναμιν δὲ ἔχει στυπτικήν, ψυκτικήν, ὠφελῶν στομαχικοὺς ἐν ποτῷ ἀμβλεῖς τε τοῖς αἰσθητηρίοις· ποιεῖ καὶ πρὸς τὰ ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς ῥεύματα καὶ ἕλκη σὴν γάλακτι. δοκεῖ δὲ καὶ ὠκυτόκιος εἶναι καὶ φυλακτήριος τῶν συνειληφυιῶν περιαπτόμενος.
entry_en: There is a stone found in Samian earth which goldsmiths use for smoothing and polishing. It is excellent when white and massive. It has astringent and cooling properties. It benefits, in a drink, those suffering from stomach ailments and it dulls the senses. It is good with milk both for rheums in the eyes and for sores. It seems to speed childbirth and to protect pregnant women when hung as an amulet.

entry_gr: καὶ τῆς Χίας δὲ τὴν λευκὴν καὶ ὑπότεφρον παραλημπτέον καὶ τῇ Σαμίᾳ ἐμφερῆ. πλακώδης δέ ἐστι καὶ λεπτή, τοῖς τε σχήμασι τῆς ἀναπλάσεως διαφέρουσα. δύναμιν δὲ τὴν αὐτὴν ἔχει τῇ Σαμίᾳ. τετανὸν δὲ καὶ στίλβον, ἔτι δὲ εὔχρουν τὸ πρόσωπον καὶ ὅλον τὸ σῶμα ἀποτελεῖ, σμήχει δὲ ἀντὶ νίτρου ἐν βαλανείῳ. τὰ δὲ αὐτὰ καὶ ἡ Σελινουσία γῆ ποιεῖ, ἀρίστη δέ ἐστιν 2 ἡ ἄγαν λευκὴ καὶ στίλβουσα, εὐθρυβής τε καὶ ταχέως χυλουμένη, ἐπειδὰν ὑγρὸν λάβη.
entry_en: 1. And of the Chian earth you must take that which is white, somewhat ash-colored, and resembling Samian earth. It is laminated, fine, and it comes in various shapes. It has the same properties as Samian earth. It makes the face and the entire body smooth, shiny, and healthy looking, and in the bath it cleanses like soda. 2. Selinus earth also accomplishes the same things. That which is very white, shiny, crumbly, and dissolves quickly if it should get wet is excellent.

entry_gr: τῆς δὲ Κιμωλίας ἡ μέν ἐστι λευκὴ ἡ δὲ ἐμπόρφυρος καὶ λιπαρίαν τινὰ ἔμφυτον κεκτημένη, πρός τε τὴν ἁρὴν κατάψυχρος, ἣν ἀρίστην ἡγητέον. ἑκάτεραι δὲ διαφοροῦσιν ὄξει διειμέναι παρωτίδας καὶ τὰ ἄλλα φύματα, πρός τε τὰ πυρίκαυτα ποιοῦσιν ἐπιχριόμεναι παραχρῆμα, ὥστε ἀφλυκταίνωτα διατηρεῖν τὰ πεπονθότα μέρη. καταστέλλουσι δὲ καὶ διδύμων σκληρίας καὶ φλεγμονὰς τὰς περὶ 2 ὅλον τὸ σῶμα, ἔτι δὲ ἐρυσιπέλασιν ἐνίστανται. καθόλου δὲ πολύχρηστοί εἰσιν αἱ γνήσιοι, ἐὰν μὴ νόθοι παραλαμβάνωνται.
entry_en: 1. One kind of Cimolian earth is white and the other purplish, having some inherent greasiness and being quite cold to the touch; it must be judged the best. Both kinds dissolve tumors of the parotid glands and the other growths when diluted in vinegar, and they operate on bums so that they maintain the afflicted areas free of blisters if smeared on them right away. 2. They reduce both testicular indurations and inflammations all over the body; additionally, they prevail over erysipelas. In general, genuine Cimolian earths are extremely useful unless one used the counterfeit.

entry_gr: ἡ δὲ λεγομένη πνιγῖτις γῆ τῇ μὲν χρόᾳ ἔοικέ πως τῇ Ἐρετριάδι, ἔστι δὲ ἁδρόβωλος καὶ ψυκτικὴ πρὸς τὰς τῶν χειρῶν ἐπιβολάς, τῇ δὲ γλώσση μάλιστα κολλᾶται ὡς ἐκκρέμασθαι. δύναμιν δὲ ἔχει τὴν αὐτὴν τῇ Κιμωλίᾳ, βραχὺ τῆς εὐτονίας ὑστεροῦσα. ταύτην ἀντὶ τῆς Ἐρετριάδος τινὲς πιπράσκουσιν.
entry_en: The earth called pnigitis is somewhat similar to the Eretrian earth in color, but it comes in large clods, it cools the hands that touch it, and it sticks so tightly to the tongue as to hang from it. It has the same properties as Cimolian earth, although it falls slightly short of it in strength. Some sell it as Eretrian earth.

entry_gr: ὄστρακα δὲ τὰ ἐξ ἰπνῶν τὰ λίαν κάτοπτα ἐσχαραωτικά, ὅθεν ἐπιχριόμενα σὺν ὄξει κνησμοὺς καὶ ἐξανθήματα ἰᾶται καὶ ποδαγρικοὺς ὠφελεῖ, ἀναλημφθέντα δὲ κηρωτῇ χοιράδας διαφορεῖ. καὶ ἡ ἐκ τῶν καμίνων δὲ κάτοπτος γῆ πυρρὰ τὴν αὐτὴν ἔχει δύναμιν τοῖς ὀστράκοις.
entry_en: When thoroughly burned potsherds from furnaces cicatrize. Therefore, when plastered on with vinegar they treat itching and pustules, they are beneficial to the gouty, and when compounded with cerate they dissolve scrofulous swellings of the glands. Even the dried-up red earth from the furnaces has the same properties as the potsherds.

entry_gr: ἡ δὲ Μηλία τὴν μὲν χρόαν καὶ αὐτή ἐστιν ἐμφερὴς Ἐρετριάδι γῇ τῇ σποδοειδεῖ, ἔντραχυς δὲ καὶ παρατριβομένη τοῖς δακτύλοις ὡσεὶ ψιθυρισμόν τινα ἀποτελεῖ ὅμοιον ψωχομένῃ κισήρει· τῇ δὲ δυνάμει στυπτηριώδης ἐστίν, ἀνειμένως δὲ μᾶλλον, δ δὴ καὶ διὰ τῆς γεύσεως ἐμφαίνει· ἀναξηραίνει δὲ καὶ τὴν γλῶσσαν πραέως. 2 δύναται δὲ καθαρὸν καὶ εὔχρουν ἀποτελεῖν τὸ σῶμα, λεπτύνειν τε τάς τρίχας, καὶ ἀλφοὺς καὶ λέπρας σμήχειν. χρησίμη δὲ καὶ ζωγράφοις εἰς πλείονα παραμονὴν χρωμάτων, καὶ χλωραῖς δυνάμεσι συνεργεῖ. καὶ ταύτης δὲ καὶ κοινῶς ἀπάσης γῆς τὴν ἄλιθον ἐκλεκτέον καὶ πρόσφατον, μαλακήν τε καὶ εὐθρυβῆ καὶ εὔλυτον, ὅταν ὑγροῦ θίγῃ.
entry_en: Melian earth also resembles Eretrian earth in color, that is to say the Eretrian earth that is ash-colored, but it is coarse, and when rubbed between the fingers it makes something like a whisper resembling a pumice stone being reduced into small pieces. It has the same properties as alum but quite milder, as is evident also from its taste. It also dries moderately the tongue. It can cleanse the body and give it a nice color, thin the hair, and cleanse dull-white leprosies and leprosies. It is also useful to painters in prolonging the life of colors and operates as a fixative of greens. This one, and in general all clays, must be chosen free of stones, fresh, soft, and crumbly, and they should dissolve easily when water touches them.

entry_gr: τῆς δὲ ἀμπελίτιδος γῆς, ἥν τινες φαρμακῖτιν καλοῦσι, γεννωμένης δὲ ἐν Σελευκείᾳ τῇ κατὰ Συρίαν, τὴν μέλαιναν προκριτέον καὶ πευκίνοις ἄνθραξι μακροῖς ἐμφερῆ, ὑποσχιδακώδη τε καὶ στίλβουσαν ποσῶς, ἔτι δὲ οὐ βραδέως τηκομένην, ὅταν λεανθείσῃ ἐπιχυθῇ ποσὸν ἔλαιον. τὴν δὲ λεπτὴν καὶ τεφρώδη καὶ ἄτηκτον φαύλην ἡγητέον. δύναμιν δὲ ἔχει διαλυτικὴν καὶ ψυκτικήν· παραλαμβάνεται 2 δὲ καὶ πρὸς καλλιβλέφαρα καὶ βαφὰς τριχῶν καὶ τὰς τῶν ἀμπέλων χρίσεις πρὸς τὴν τῆς ἐκβλαστήσεως ὥραν, κτείνουσα τοὺς ἐπιγινομένους σκώληκας.
entry_en: 1. Of the earth ampelitis, which some people call pharmacitis and which is produced in Seleucia of Syria, you must choose that which is black, resembling elongated pine coals, tending to splinter, and quite shiny. Furthermore, it should not dissolve slowly when some oil is poured over it during trituration. You must judge as unacceptable that which is light, ash-like, and insoluble. 2. It has relaxing and cooling properties. It is used for painting eyelids and eyelashes, for coloring hair, and for smearing on vines at budding time, killing the worms that grow on them.

entry_gr: ἀσβόλη, ἧ οἱ ζωγράφοι χρῶνται, λαμβάνεται μὲν ἐκ τῶν ὑελουργείων· διαφέρει γὰρ αὕτη. δύναμιν δὲ ἔχει σηπτικήν στυπτικήν. ἀπουλοῖ δὲ καὶ κατακαύματα σὺν ῥοδίνη κηρωτῇ.
entry_en: The soot that painters use is taken from glass-making factories, for this is the best. It has putrefactive and astringent properties. It also cicatrizes burns when used with rose cerate.

entry_gr: μέλαν, ᾧ γράφομεν, σκευάζεται ἐκ λιγνύος συναγομένης ἐκ δᾳδίων· μείγνυνται δὲ πρὸς οὐγγίαν α΄ τοῦ κόμμεως οὐγγίαι γ΄ λιγνύος. σκευάζεται δὲ καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς ῥητίνης λιγνύος καὶ ἐκ τῆς προειρημένης ζωγραφικῆς ἀσβόλης· δεῖ δὲ τῆς μὲν ἀσβόλης μνᾶν μίαν λαμβάνειν, κόμμεως δὲ λίτραν μίαν ἡμίσειαν, ταυροκόλλης οὐγγίαν μίαν ἡμίσειαν, χαλκάνθου οὐγγίαν μίαν ἡμίσειαν. 2 ἁρμόζει δὲ εἴς τε σηπτάς καὶ πυρίκαυτα καταχριόμενον μεθ᾿ ὕδατος παχὺ καὶ ἐώμενον ἄχρις ἀπουλώσεως· καταπίπτει γάρ αὐτόματον ὑγιασθέντων τῶν ἑλκῶν. καὶ δὴ σχεδὸν ἐφ᾿ ὅσον ἱκανὸν ἐδόξαμεν, φίλτατε Ἄρειε, ἅμα καὶ μήκους τῆς συντάξεως καὶ πλήθους ὕλης τε καὶ βοηθημάτων ταμιεύσασθαι, ἅλις ἔχει.

It is also made from soot of pine resin and from the painters’ soot mentioned above. You must take one mna of soot, one and one- half litra gum, one and one-half litra bulls’ hide glue, and one and one-half litra copper sulfate. 2. It is good for putrefactive medications and for burns, being smeared on thick with water and left alone until cicatrization; for it automatically falls off once the sores have healed.
